entities.summary:
Śaunaka was a celebrated Sanskrit grammarian and teacher of the Vedic period, renowned for his extensive contributions to the Atharvaveda and his synthesis of the Bashkala and Shakala Shakhas of the Rigveda. His most notable works include the Ṛgveda-Prātiśākhya, the Bṛhaddevatā, the Caraṇa-vyūha, and six Anukramaṇīs to the Rigveda.

He is also identified as the son of Ruru and Pramadvara in the Mahabarata and the Bhagavata Purana, and is said to have taught Katyayana and Ashvalayana. His teachings had a significant impact on the development of Vedic scholarship and the transmission of Sanskrit texts.

Śaunaka's legacy extends to the preservation and study of ancient Indian texts, and his works continue to be studied and revered by scholars today.

The exact dates of Śaunaka's birth and death are unknown, but his influence on the Vedic period is undeniable.
